text:
maya: heads up — noticed a spike in mTLS handshake failures from eu-west services around 09:07 UTC, looks correlated with keystore access errors in the proxy logs.
owen: saw that too, rolling RBAC change to keystore-reader was applied ~09:05. Could be a permission timing issue.
chris_s: logs? snippets?
maya: paste from proxy (redacted):
```
2026-03-23T09:07:12Z proxy-1 ERROR mTLS: handshake failed: kms.decrypt: AccessDenied: access denied for keystore arn:aws:kms:eu-west-1:123:key/abc
    at kms.UnwrapKey (keystore.go:214)
    at proxy/handshake (handshake.go:98)
```
lee: we also see 403s from keystore-api: `{"error":"forbidden","reason":"missing: keystore.decrypt"}`
oncall: oncall paging — are services still degraded?
own: some services fallback to lower-tier model, but user-facing latency increased and a few failed requests. Scope limited to eu-west region.
maya: audit logs show a batch RBAC role prune at 09:04 from `infra-ops` job. The role removed `keystore:callDecrypt` from a service account group that proxies use.
chris_s: ohhh. Did the job include shadow mode?
own: not in that run — it was a follow-up to yesterday's policy tighten. Looks like a lifecycle script trimmed a group binding.
lee: immediate mitigation options: 1) rollback RBAC change, 2) add a temporary role binding, 3) enable a decrypt proxy fallback to regional KMS in another account. Which fastest?
maya: rollback is fastest — but need approval from infra-ops. Rolling binding back should restore decrypts in <30s.
chris_s: i'm +1 for binding revert. I'll open a revert PR and ping infra-ops.
own: meanwhile can we add an emergency audit log filter and retention marker so we don't lose the exact API call traces?
maya: added an audit tag `incident-1719897654` to CloudTrail and keystore logs at 09:12 UTC.
infra-bot: deploybot: Revert PR created by chris_s at https://git.internal/repo/infra/keystore-rbac/pull/418 — CI passing.
lee: @infra-ops please approve revert, urgent. :rotating_light:
oncall: approve?
infra-ops (via infra-bot): approved the revert at 09:14 UTC.
own: reverted binding applied at 09:15:03, observed decrypt success spikes after 09:15:10. Handshake failure rate dropped ~92% by 09:17.
maya: marking incident as mitigated for now — we should still run a root cause: why did the prune include the proxy group?
chris_s: root cause hypothesis: our RBAC prune script uses group name regexes and a stale alias mapping caused the proxy group to match.
lee: follow-ups: 1) add canary mode to RBAC prune runs (dry run + alert on any service-account-group removals), 2) stricter tests in CI to prevent removal of groups with `keystore` access, 3) add edge fallback in proxy to avoid immediate fail-open but queue decrypts for retry, 4) surface keystore audit events in console with quick filters.
own: also recommend temporary increase of audit retention for keystore/API logs for 30 days for postmortem.
maya: agreed. I'll file a postmortem template and link logs.
chris_s: file opened: https://pm.internal/incidents/INC-2026-03123 — assigning to @lee for RCA and @owen for RBAC script changes.
lee: will triage tomorrow, but quick question: do we want to add an automated test that runs a simulated mTLS handshake using service account tokens before any RBAC prune?
own: yes, a pre-prune canary that performs `kms:Decrypt` calls against a synthetic keystore in each region. If any fail, abort.
infra-bot: alert: scheduled job `rbac-prune` will be paused until 2026-03-25T00:00Z for safety.
maya: thanks. TL;DR: cause = RBAC prune removed decrypt permission from proxy group in eu-west; impact = mTLS handshakes failed -> degraded services; mitigation = revert binding; action items created. :white_check_mark: 
lee: adding one more: improve error classification so proxy returns 5xx vs 4xx appropriately (AccessDenied -> 5xx for transient perms?) thoughts?
own: AccessDenied should be 403 so caller knows it's an auth issue; but proxy can surface a more specific diagnostic and trigger automated RBAC rollback keyboard if it detects bulk access denied across many nodes.
maya: agreed — add monitoring rule: if >10% of proxies in region see KMS AccessDenied within 2m, trigger an alert and optional auto-revert.
chris_s: OK I'll draft the monitoring playbook and include sample detection query:
```
count_over_time(kms_decrypt_errors{region="eu-west",reason="AccessDenied"}[2m]) / count_up(kms_proxy_up{region="eu-west"}) > 0.1
```
lee: good. Any compliance notes? We changed RBAC; audit trail exists, no data exfil. SOC?
maya: SOC notified via pagerduty, they want the audit bundle and timeline. I'll attach to incident.
oncall: closing thread for now — re-open if we see new spikes. :pray:
